long_biography.plain_text:
Born in Aguadilla, Carlos Delgado developed as a left-handed hitter with encouragement from his father. He signed with the Toronto Blue Jays and became one of the club's leading sluggers, later playing for the Florida Marlins and New York Mets. His sustained major-league career generated substantial salary income, while his 473 home runs remain a defining achievement for a Puerto Rican player.

Delgado founded Extra Bases in 2001 to support children and charitable organisations, especially in Puerto Rico. The foundation has funded community and health initiatives alongside his personal donations. After retiring from professional play, he has remained active in its work and in public baseball conversations, rather than being identified with a separate current operating business.
